key_insight: An agent can help transfer and refine experimental strategies across different quantum processors, enabling the same quantum task to be executed successfully on multiple devices.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical route to scale quantum experimentation beyond single-device expertise by combining automated decision-making with human operator intervention.
method: Developed an experimental strategy on one three-qubit NMR processor and deployed it sequentially to four others.
Used an agent to assess evidence, choose the next measurements, and adapt the procedure during Grover state preparation.
Combined device-specific calibration, control-pulse optimization, and measurement at each processor.
evidence_signal: Across four processors, the reconstructed dominant eigenstates produced marked-state populations between 0.910 and 0.959, with relative deviations below 3.8% from the ideal value of 0.945.
watch_item: The approach still depends on operator preparation and physical intervention, so full autonomy and transferability may be limited by hardware-specific constraints and drift.
paper_title: Agent-assisted experimental strategy transfer across quantum processors
